items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: those are the years I was doing things with Oliver Nelson... 'More Blues and the Abstract Truth' with Ollie

ctx.x: Okay. But there’s still — your name was obviously getting around as a —

Yeah those are the years I was doing things with Oliver Nelson. Some of the best recordings I ever made I thought. “Alfie” with Sonny Rollins, “Bumpin’” with Wes Montgomery, and “More Blues and the Abstract Truth” with Ollie. I mean those were really favorite times. We’d go into the studio and just eat the music alive. We’d be sight reading and playing it like we’d played it for three weeks. It was amazing, just ferocious. “More Blues and the Abstract Truth” was designed for three days and we essentially finished…
I see. Yeah he had quite a success with that, the first one, and he really made his name, didn’t he?
